proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\mu=P_{M_0}\) and \(\nu=P_{M_1}\). By hypothesis, the refinement of each \(M_j\), \(j\in\{0,1\}\), belongs to \(\mathfrak R(H,L)\). Thus \(\mathrm{def:refinement\text{-}class}\) supplies bounded refinement span, instantaneous acyclicity, and exact summary \(H\). The remaining hypotheses supply the fixed alphabet family \(\mathcal A\), its finiteness and nontriviality, semi-Markovian roots, time-homogeneous structural equations, strict stationarity, and positive finite cylinders. Applying \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\) gives
\[
 M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A).
\]

We next derive whole-law equality from cylinder equality. Let \(\mathscr E\) be the algebra of finite unions of cylinders in \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\). For any finite collection of cylinders, taking the union of their finite coordinate supports partitions \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) into finitely many cylinder atoms. Finite additivity and the hypothesis \(\mu(C_{\mathcal A})=\nu(C_{\mathcal A})\) therefore imply
\[
 \mu(E)=\nu(E)\qquad(E\in\mathscr E).
\]
Here is a direct uniqueness argument. Let \(\mathscr D\) be the smallest lambda-system containing \(\mathscr E\). For fixed \(A\in\mathscr E\), the class
\[
 \mathscr D_A=\{B\in\mathscr D:A\cap B\in\mathscr D\}
\]
is a lambda-system containing \(\mathscr E\), because \(\mathscr E\) is an algebra. Hence \(\mathscr D\subseteq\mathscr D_A\). Holding instead \(B\in\mathscr D\) fixed and repeating the same lambda-system argument in the first argument shows that \(A\cap B\in\mathscr D\) for every \(A,B\in\mathscr D\). A lambda-system closed under finite intersections is a sigma-field: complements follow from the lambda-system property, and an arbitrary countable union is converted into a disjoint countable union by successive differences. Consequently
\[
 \mathscr D=\sigma(\mathscr E),
\]
which is the product sigma-field on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\).

Now define
\[
 \mathscr C=\{B\in\sigma(\mathscr E):
 \mu(A\cap B)=\nu(A\cap B)\text{ for every }A\in\mathscr E\}.
\]
The class \(\mathscr C\) contains \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\); it is closed under complements because \(\mu(A)=\nu(A)\) for \(A\in\mathscr E\); and it is closed under countable disjoint unions by countable additivity. Thus \(\mathscr C\) is a lambda-system. Since intersections of members of \(\mathscr E\) remain in \(\mathscr E\), equality on \(\mathscr E\) implies \(\mathscr E\subseteq\mathscr C\). Hence \(\mathscr D\subseteq\mathscr C\). Taking \(A=\Omega_{\mathcal A}\in\mathscr E\) yields
\[
 \mu(B)=\nu(B)\qquad(B\in\sigma(\mathscr E)),
\]
so \(P_{M_0}=P_{M_1}\) as measures on the common path space.

Finally, the assumed strict inequality
\[
 \theta_{M_0}(y;x)\neq\theta_{M_1}(y;x)
\]
together with whole-law equality is a counterexample to the implication quantified over compatible model pairs in \(\mathrm{def:uniform\text{-}identification}\). Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{UID}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)=0.
\]
The argument verifies already constructed models on the unchanged alphabets; it performs no alphabet enlargement or model gluing.

Every directed edge of \(G^\star\) is of the form \(i_{t-\ell}\to j_t\) with \(0\leq\ell\leq L\), and its coordinate projection is an edge \(i\to j\) of the directed part \(H^{\to}\). Therefore the coordinate projection of a directed path in \(G^\star\) is a directed walk in \(H^{\to}\). Because \(H^{\to}\) is acyclic and has no directed self-loop, no coordinate can occur twice in this walk: a repeated coordinate would give a directed cycle, and two consecutive equal coordinates would give a self-loop. Hence a directed path ending at either query vertex has at most \(n-1\) edges. Each edge moves backward by at most \(L\) when the path is traced toward its ancestors. Since the query vertices occur at times \(-\gamma\) and \(0\), it follows that
\[
 A^\star:=\operatorname{an}_{G^\star}(\{X_{-\gamma},Y_0\})
 \subseteq V\times[-\gamma-(n-1)L,0].
\]
The interval on the right contains \(\gamma+(n-1)L+1\) integer times. Using \(0\leq\gamma\leq L\), we obtain
\[
 |A^\star|
 \leq n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}
 \leq n(nL+1).
\]

Fix an arbitrary \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\), and denote its refinement by \(R\). By \(\mathrm{ass:refinement\text{-}span}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:exact\text{-}summary}\), every directed or bidirected edge of \(R\) is among the corresponding lag or offset edges placed in \(G^\star\); hence \(R\subseteq G^\star\). Because \(A^\star\) is ancestral in \(G^\star\), no observed vertex outside \(A^\star\) is a directed parent of a vertex in \(A^\star\). Restricting the structural equations to \(A^\star\) thus leaves those equations unchanged. A pairwise exogenous root whose other observed child lies outside \(A^\star\) becomes a private root after marginalization, while all exogenous roots remain mutually independent by \(\mathrm{ass:semi\text{-}markovian}\). Consequently the marginal law on \(A^\star\), together with its interventions on \(X_{-\gamma}\), is generated by a finite semi-Markovian SCM compatible with the supergraph \(G^\star[A^\star]\). In particular, because the removed vertices are not ancestors of either query vertex, the restricted and original SCMs have the same distribution of \(Y_0\) under \(\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x)\).

Suppose ordinary ID on \(G^\star[A^\star]\) returns \(F\). Applying \(\mathrm{lem:ordinary\text{-}id\text{-}soundness}\) to the restricted SCM gives
\[
 F(P_M(A^\star))
 =P_M(Y_0=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x))
 =\theta_M(y;x).
\]
The set \(A^\star\) is finite. Therefore every joint cell or marginal appearing in the returned ID expression is a finite cylinder probability on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\). Marginalization over the fixed finite alphabets uses finite sums, the ID factorization uses finite products, and every conditional-kernel denominator is a finite-cylinder probability that is strictly positive by \(\mathrm{ass:cylinder\text{-}positivity}\). Thus the returned expression belongs to \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) by \(\mathrm{def:cylinder\text{-}language}\). Since \(M\) was arbitrary, the equality is uniform over \(\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\). Only the success implication was used, so an ordinary-ID failure on the saturated graph yields no conclusion here.

Write \(A_t=O_{1,t}\), \(B_t=O_{2,t}\), and \(C_t=O_{3,t}\), and, for \(s\in(0,1)\) and \(d\in\{0,1\}\), put
\[
 b_s(d)=s^d(1-s)^{1-d}.
\]
All observed variables are binary by \(\mathrm{def:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}regression}\). The two-sided structural solutions exist and are unique causal functions of their noise histories. Indeed, after substitution, model zero satisfies
\[
 B_t=(R_t\wedge B_{t-1})\oplus U_t\oplus N_t,
\]
and model one satisfies
\[
 A_t=(R'_t\wedge A_{t-1})\oplus U'_t\oplus N'_t.
\]
Whenever \(R_t=0\), respectively \(R'_t=0\), the right-hand side forgets the preceding state. Independent reset events have probability \(1/2\), so almost surely there is a reset between every fixed time and some finite time in its past. Starting at the most recent such reset constructs the solution, any two causal solutions agree from that reset onward, and the construction commutes with every integer time shift.

Let \(\mathcal H^{\mathrm{obs}}_{t-1}\) denote the observed history through time \(t-1\). In model zero, \(U_t\) is an independent fair bit, so \(A_t\) is conditionally fair given \(\mathcal H^{\mathrm{obs}}_{t-1}\). Since \(B_t=A_t\oplus N_t\), for \(a,b\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{M_0}(A_t=a,B_t=b\mid\mathcal H^{\mathrm{obs}}_{t-1})
 &=P_{M_0}(A_t=a\mid\mathcal H^{\mathrm{obs}}_{t-1})
   P(N_t=a\oplus b)\\
 &=\frac12 b_q(a\oplus b).
 \end{aligned}
\]
In model one, \(U'_t\) makes \(B_t\) conditionally fair and \(A_t=B_t\oplus N'_t\), which yields the same conditional mass. Hence, in both models, the pairs \((A_t,B_t)\) are independent over time with common mass
\[
 \pi(a,b)=\frac12 b_q(a\oplus b).
\]
In both models the remaining equation gives
\[
 P(C_t=c\mid(A_s,B_s)_{s\in\mathbb Z},(C_s)_{s<t})
 =b_r(c\oplus B_{t-1}).
\]
Thus both observed processes have the same explicit representation: draw the pairs \((A_t,B_t)\) independently with mass \(\pi\), draw \(E_t\) independently with success probability \(r\), and set \(C_t=B_{t-1}\oplus E_t\). For a complete cylinder on an integer interval \([u,v]\), its probability is
\[
 \sum_{b_{u-1}\in\{0,1\}}\frac12
 \prod_{t=u}^{v}\pi(a_t,b_t)b_r(c_t\oplus b_{t-1}).
\]
Summing this expression over unspecified cells gives every finite-cylinder probability. The formula is identical in the two models and invariant under translating \([u,v]\), proving equality on all cylinders and strict stationarity. Since \(q=1/5\) and \(r=1/10\), every factor in every complete-cylinder formula is positive; a nonempty finite sum of such terms proves positivity of every finite cylinder.

It remains to verify the graphs. In model zero, the structural functions genuinely depend on the observed parents in the edges
\[
 B_{t-1}\to A_t,\qquad A_t\to B_t,\qquad B_{t-1}\to C_t.
\]
In model one, the corresponding edges are
\[
 A_{t-1}\to B_t,\qquad B_t\to A_t,\qquad B_{t-1}\to C_t.
\]
The positive support of the displayed noises ensures that none of these functional dependences is degenerate. Each instantaneous slice contains only one of \(A_t\to B_t\) and \(B_t\to A_t\), so it is acyclic. Every directed lag is zero or one. The primitive noise sequences are mutually independent and each noise has only one observed child, so there is no bidirected edge. Translation invariance of the edge templates and the time-homogeneous equations give in both cases the exact common summary
\[
 1\to2,\qquad 2\to1,\qquad 2\to3,
\]
with no bidirected edge. Together with the already established binary support, stationarity, and cylinder positivity, \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\) gives
\[
 M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,1,\mathcal A).
\]

Under \(\operatorname{do}(A_{-1}=0)\) in model zero, the two relevant equations reduce to
\[
 B_{-1}=N_{-1},\qquad C_0=N_{-1}\oplus E_0.
\]
Independence therefore yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{M_0}(C_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(A_{-1}=0))
 &=q(1-r)+(1-q)r\\
 &=q+r-2qr=\frac15+\frac1{10}-\frac2{50}=\frac{13}{50}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
In model one, \(A_{-1}\) is a child of \(B_{-1}\). Replacing the structural equation for \(A_{-1}\) does not alter the fair distribution of \(B_{-1}\), which is the observed parent of \(C_0\). Hence
\[
 P_{M_1}(C_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(A_{-1}=0))
 =\frac12(1-r)+\frac12r=\frac12.
\]

Finally, each effect is identifiable when its refinement is known. In model zero the relevant directed chain is \(A_{-1}\to B_{-1}\to C_0\), and the independent-noise factorization gives the do-free functional
\[
 \sum_{b\in\{0,1\}}P(C_0=1\mid B_{-1}=b)P(B_{-1}=b\mid A_{-1}=0).
\]
In model one there is no directed path from \(A_{-1}\) to \(C_0\), so intervention leaves the outcome marginal unchanged and the functional is \(P(C_0=1)\). Cylinder positivity makes the conditional functional well defined. Thus the refinements are individually identifiable even though their common entire observed law cannot determine which of the unequal effects, \(13/50\) or \(1/2\), is the target.

At this point every premise of \(\mathrm{lem:stationary\text{-}lift}\) has been verified: the two final SCMs have refinements in the same exact class, fixed common alphabets, the required structural and stationarity properties, positive cylinders, identical probabilities for all finite cylinders, and unequal target effects. That lemma therefore yields
\[
 P_{M_0}=P_{M_1}\qquad\text{as measures on }\Omega_{\mathcal A}.
\]

Define
\[
 N_\star=n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}.
\]
Each of the four ordered top-level rules in \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\) is a finite computation. The first two compare the input with fixed finite templates. The third uses finite ancestry, descendant, simple-path, and directed-cycle searches on \(H\), followed, on success, by a finite sum over the fixed finite alphabet. For the fourth rule, \(\mathrm{prop:acyclic\text{-}summary\text{-}reduction}\) puts the ancestral ADMG on at most \(N_\star\) vertices. A memoized ID state assigns each such vertex one of the three labels absent, random, and fixed. There are at most \(3^{N_\star}\) such assignments, and the definition forbids revisiting a state. Counting initialization once, the four ordered top-level rule evaluations once each, and all possible memo states gives
\[
 1+4+3^{N_\star}
 =5+3^{n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}}
 =B_\star(n,L,\gamma).
\]
Every branch returns immediately with one tag, and the residual branch returns \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\). The finite ordered deterministic rules therefore terminate within this bound and emit exactly one of \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}\), \(\operatorname{FAIL}\), and \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\).

We verify success soundness branch by branch. On \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{out}}\), \(\mathrm{prop:outside\text{-}witness\text{-}identification}\) proves
\[
 F_{\mathrm{out}}(P_M)=\theta_M(1;0)
 \qquad\text{for every }M\in\mathfrak M(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}}),
\]
and its displayed expression is in \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}})\) by positivity. If neither special branch has matched and \(\mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,X,Y,\gamma)\) holds, \(\mathrm{prop:scg\text{-}adjustment\text{-}transfer}\) gives
\[
 F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A),
 \qquad
 F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(P_M;y,x)=\theta_M(y;x)
 \quad(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)).
\]
This covers eligible cyclic and self-looped directed summaries as well as acyclic ones. Finally, if the acyclic, loop-free fallback reaches an ordinary-ID success, \(\mathrm{prop:acyclic\text{-}summary\text{-}reduction}\) proves
\[
 F\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A),
 \qquad F(P_M)=\theta_M(y;x)
 \quad(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)).
\]
These are all success branches, so every success is uniformly sound.

The sole failure branch emits the rational structural tables and noise laws in \(\mathrm{def:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}regression}\). Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}collision}\) proves that they directly define two final models on the unchanged binary alphabets with
\[
 M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,1,\mathcal A),
 \qquad P_{M_0}=P_{M_1}\text{ on }\Omega_{\mathcal A},
\]
but
\[
 \theta_{M_0}(1;0)=\frac{13}{50}\neq\frac12=\theta_{M_1}(1;0).
\]
Equivalently, \(\mathrm{lem:stationary\text{-}lift}\) applies to this directly constructed pair and certifies \(\operatorname{UID}=0\). Thus every failure is sound.

For completeness of the one-way semantic implications, suppose the output is \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\) and two compatible models have the same entire observed law. Their probabilities agree for every cylinder occurring in \(F\), so the finite arithmetic expression has the same value under both laws. Success soundness identifies that common value with each target, and \(\mathrm{def:uniform\text{-}identification}\) gives \(\operatorname{UID}=1\). On failure, the displayed pair violates the implication in that definition, so \(\operatorname{UID}=0\). All cases not covered by a sound success or the one direct failure return \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\); hence neither converse is asserted.

For \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{out}}\), the coordinate set is \(V=\{X,Y\}\). Every member of \(\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}\) would, by \(\mathrm{def:micro\text{-}frontdoor\text{-}family}\), have to contain a nonempty mediator-role set satisfying
\[
 \varnothing\neq\mathcal D
 \subseteq(V\setminus\{X,Y\})\times[-b,0].
\]
The set on the right is empty. Therefore
\[
 \mathfrak F_{\mathrm{FD}}(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}},1,2,1)
 =\varnothing.
\]
The first ordered rule of \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\) matches this exact input before any later branch and returns
\[
 \operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,
 \mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}},1,2,1,0,1)
 =\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{out}}).
\]
By \(\mathrm{prop:outside\text{-}witness\text{-}identification}\), for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H_{\mathrm{out}},1,\mathcal A^{\mathrm{bin}})\),
\[
 F_{\mathrm{out}}(P_M)
 =P_M(Y_0=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-1}=0)).
\]
This proves a successful input outside the defined front-door family. The conclusion is only this witnessed strict separation; it neither asserts that all front-door certificates are implemented nor asserts a general embedding of another certificate family.

Condition on the event that the procedure returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\). Success soundness in the corrected \(\mathrm{thm:tid\text{-}dichotomy}\) gives the identifying equality
\[
 F(p_F)=\theta_M(y;x)
 \qquad(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)).
\]
This is the only step connecting the causal target to the observed-law functional.

To verify the sampling inputs, let \(a_-\) and \(a_+\) be respectively the smallest and largest time offsets appearing in the finite supports of the cylinders in \(\mathcal C_{F,\mathcal A}\), and put \(w=a_+-a_-\). Then \(Z_t\) is measurable with respect to the observed block from time \(t+a_-\) through time \(t+a_+\), and \(\lVert Z_t\rVert\leq\sqrt{d_F}\). Thus all moments required for the finite-dimensional central limit and HAC statements are finite. Moreover, for \(k>w\), monotonicity of absolute-regularity coefficients under measurable maps and restriction of sigma-fields gives
\[
 \beta_Z(k)
 \leq\beta_M(k-w)
 \leq C_\beta\rho^{k-w}.
\]
Hence the shifted cylinder-indicator process is itself geometrically beta mixing. Strict stationarity of \(P_M\) makes \((Z_t)\) strictly stationary. Cylinder positivity makes every population denominator in the rational expression \(F\) positive. The event that all corresponding empirical denominators are positive has probability tending to one, as stated in \(\mathrm{lem:valid\text{-}cylinder\text{-}hac\text{-}delta}\). Omitting the fixed number of shifts lost at the two trajectory boundaries changes the empirical mean by \(O(T^{-1})\) and the lag-window covariance by \(O(h_T/T)=o(1)\), so it does not change the limits.

The hypotheses \(K(u)=(1-|u|)\mathbf 1\{|u|\leq1\}\), \(h_T\to\infty\), \(h_T=o(T^{1/4})\), and \(v_F>0\) are exactly \(\mathrm{ass:hac\text{-}kernel}\), \(\mathrm{ass:hac\text{-}bandwidth}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:variance\text{-}nondegeneracy}\). All premises of \(\mathrm{lem:valid\text{-}cylinder\text{-}hac\text{-}delta}\) are therefore satisfied. Applying it and substituting the identifying equality above yields
\[
 \widehat\Omega_F\overset p\longrightarrow\Omega_F,
\]
\[
 \sqrt T\{\widehat\theta_F-\theta_M(y;x)\}
 \Rightarrow N(0,v_F),
 \qquad
 \widehat v_F\overset p\longrightarrow v_F,
\]
and
\[
 P_M\!\left\{\theta_M(y;x)\in
 \left[\widehat\theta_F\pm
 z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat v_F/T}\right]\right\}
 \longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\]
The same lemma proves that replacing \(F\) by an algebraically equivalent cylinder expression gives the same delta-method limit after redundant coordinates imposed by the probability simplex are removed. Thus every asserted limit is conditional on a sound identification output and does not attach an inferential target to an \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\) query.

Assume \(L=0\). Since \(0\leq\gamma\leq L\), necessarily \(\gamma=0\). By \(\mathrm{ass:refinement\text{-}span}\), every directed edge and every shared-root relation has offset zero. Stationarity of a refinement translates each such relation through all integer times, while \(\mathrm{ass:exact\text{-}summary}\) fixes its coordinate pair. Hence each feasible refinement is the translation closure of the finite static ADMG specified by \(H\). If the directed part of \(H\) contained a directed cycle or a directed self-loop, its time-zero copy would violate \(\mathrm{ass:instantaneous\text{-}acyclicity}\). Therefore \(H^{\to}\) is acyclic and loop-free.

The first two special rules of \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\) require their displayed lag-one inputs, so neither matches an input with \(L=0\). There are now two cases. If
\[
 \mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,X,Y,0)=\mathsf{true},
\]
the third rule returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}})\). Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:scg\text{-}adjustment\text{-}transfer}\) proves that this is a finite-cylinder functional and that
\[
 F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(P_M;y,x)=\theta_M(y;x)
 \qquad(M\in\mathfrak M(H,0,\mathcal A)).
\]

If the adjustment predicate is false, the acyclic, loop-free property just proved forces the fourth rule to apply. At \(L=0\), the saturated time-unrolled ancestral graph has only time-zero vertices and is exactly the relevant ancestral subgraph of the static ADMG. The procedure makes its one memoized ordinary-ID call there. If ID returns \(F\), \(\mathrm{prop:acyclic\text{-}summary\text{-}reduction}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,0,\mathcal A,X,Y,0,x,y)
 =\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F),
 \qquad F(P_M)=\theta_M(y;x)
\]
for every compatible \(M\). If ID fails, the fourth rule returns \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\). Thus a zero-lag input is handled by the earlier adjustment success when eligible and otherwise by exactly one ordinary-ID call; no failure of ID is converted into a fixed-alphabet stationary hedge certificate.

Consider the fixed finite set of queries on which \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}\) returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_j)\), \(1\leq j\leq m\). By the corrected \(\mathrm{thm:tid\text{-}dichotomy}\), each returned functional is a finite-cylinder observed-law map satisfying
\[
 \theta_j=F_j(p_{F_j})
\]
throughout the compatible model class. Under the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{thm:cylinder\text{-}hac}\), each plug-in estimator is consistent, so
\[
 \widehat\theta_{F_j}-\theta_j\overset p\longrightarrow0
 \qquad(1\leq j\leq m).
\]
Because \(m\) is fixed and finite, a union bound gives
\[
 \max_{1\leq j\leq m}|\widehat\theta_{F_j}-\theta_j|
 \overset p\longrightarrow0.
\]
If \(\Delta=\min_{j\neq k}|\theta_j-\theta_k|>0\), then on the event that this maximum is smaller than \(\Delta/2\), every pairwise sign
\[
 \operatorname{sign}(\widehat\theta_{F_j}-\widehat\theta_{F_k})
 =\operatorname{sign}(\theta_j-\theta_k)
\]
is correct. The probability of that event tends to one. This is also exactly the conclusion of \(\mathrm{prop:finite\text{-}margin\text{-}plugin\text{-}ranking}\).

On a \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) output, \(\mathrm{thm:tid\text{-}dichotomy}\) supplies the directly constructed fixed-alphabet pair having the same observed process law and unequal causal scores, so no observed-law ranking can assign a unique target there. An \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\) output carries no identifying or nonidentifying assertion. Excluding both tags therefore ranks precisely the certified causal scores and records, rather than conceals, the reason for every exclusion.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every feasible \((H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)\), the certified partial procedure \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}\) in \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\) terminates after at most \(B_\star(n,L,\gamma)=5+3^{n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}}\) transitions and emits exactly one of \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\), \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lag}}(\mathcal A))\), or \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\). Every success has \(F\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) and \(F(P_M)=\theta_M(y;x)\) for all \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\). Every failure encodes two final models \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\) on the fixed alphabets such that \(P_{M_0}=P_{M_1}\) on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) and \(\theta_{M_0}(y;x)\neq\theta_{M_1}(y;x)\). Consequently success implies \(\operatorname{UID}=1\), failure implies \(\operatorname{UID}=0\), and no converse is claimed. The procedure returns the displayed success on \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{out}}\), the displayed failure on the binary lag-switch query in \(\mathrm{def:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}regression}\), returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}})\) when neither special branch matches and \(\mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,X,Y,\gamma)\) holds, and otherwise uses one saturated ordinary-ID call when the directed part of \(H\) is acyclic and loop-free; unresolved cases return \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current bound omits the newly inserted adjustment rule. Under the transition convention in \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\), initialization plus four ordered top-level evaluations contributes five transitions before the memoized ID states, so the current bound with constant four is false. The revised statement gives the weaker correct bound and records the adjustment success branch.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For fixed \(\mathcal A\), when \(L=0\), every feasible refinement is the translation closure of one finite static ADMG on \(V\), and \(\gamma=0\). The first two lag-one special branches of \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,0,\mathcal A,X,Y,0,x,y)\) cannot match. If \(\mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,X,Y,0)\) holds, the procedure returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}})\), which is uniformly valid. Otherwise it makes one ordinary-ID call on the relevant ancestral subgraph. If ID succeeds, it returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\), where \(F\) is the ordinary-ID functional on the common product alphabet; if ID fails, it returns \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\). No fixed-alphabet stationary hedge lift is claimed on the ID-failure branch.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current statement incorrectly says that every zero-lag input makes an ordinary ID call. The ordered procedure first returns the published adjustment functional whenever \(\mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}\) holds; ordinary ID is called only when that predicate is false. The revised case split is the exact weaker claim implemented by the procedure.

proposed.statement: For every feasible \((H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)\), the certified partial procedure \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}\) in \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\) terminates after at most \(B_\star(n,L,\gamma)=5+3^{n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}}\) transitions and emits exactly one of \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\), \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lag}}(\mathcal A))\), or \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\). Every success has \(F\in\mathcal L_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\mathcal A)\) and \(F(P_M)=\theta_M(y;x)\) for all \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\). Every failure encodes two final models \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\) on the fixed alphabets such that \(P_{M_0}=P_{M_1}\) on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) and \(\theta_{M_0}(y;x)\neq\theta_{M_1}(y;x)\). Consequently success implies \(\operatorname{UID}=1\), failure implies \(\operatorname{UID}=0\), and no converse is claimed. The procedure returns the displayed success on \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{out}}\), the displayed failure on the binary lag-switch query in \(\mathrm{def:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}regression}\), returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}})\) when neither special branch matches and \(\mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,X,Y,\gamma)\) holds, and otherwise uses one saturated ordinary-ID call when the directed part of \(H\) is acyclic and loop-free; unresolved cases return \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\).
proposed.justification: The narrowed theorem proves termination and soundness for the four-rule, three-way partial procedure, including the published adjustment success branch.
proposed.gap: Neither success nor failure is complete for all feasible inputs.
proposed.consumer: EasyRCA uses success, displays certified failure, and separately reports unknown.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The corrected claim needs the load-bearing adjustment-transfer proposition in its proof spine and must keep the theorem metadata synchronized with the fourth ordered rule.

proposed.statement: For fixed \(\mathcal A\), when \(L=0\), every feasible refinement is the translation closure of one finite static ADMG on \(V\), and \(\gamma=0\). The first two lag-one special branches of \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,0,\mathcal A,X,Y,0,x,y)\) cannot match. If \(\mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,X,Y,0)\) holds, the procedure returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}})\), which is uniformly valid. Otherwise it makes one ordinary-ID call on the relevant ancestral subgraph. If ID succeeds, it returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\), where \(F\) is the ordinary-ID functional on the common product alphabet; if ID fails, it returns \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\). No fixed-alphabet stationary hedge lift is claimed on the ID-failure branch.
proposed.justification: At zero lag the procedure uses the sound adjustment branch when eligible and otherwise reduces to one ordinary ID call.
proposed.gap: An ordinary-ID failure returns unknown because the fixed-alphabet stationary hedge lift is unproved.
proposed.consumer: Static users receive either a valid adjustment or ordinary-ID success without an unsafe failure claim.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The replacement adds the adjustment-transfer dependency required by the corrected zero-lag case split and removes the stale assertion that ordinary ID is always called.
